stocks.discussion_driver: Western Digital fell ~7% on July 1 alongside Micron and SanDisk in a broad memory sector selloff driven by profit-taking after a 240% YTD surge on AI data center demand. Citrini Research flagged potential AI-efficiency headwinds that could reduce hyperscaler memory consumption, cooling sentiment. The pullback follows WDC's 52-week high of $799.87 in mid-June, a Fox Advisors downgrade citing HDD pricing expectations running ahead of fundamentals, and a sharp 13.2% drop on June 26 before a 10.2% partial recovery on June 29.
bull_case: AI/cloud data center demand for HDDs and NAND is driving record revenue — Q3 FY2026 hit $3.34B (+46% YoY) with net income up 320%, and a global memory shortage is expected to persist into 2027-2028 supporting sustained pricing power.

Multiple tier-1 analysts remain bullish: Cantor Fitzgerald raised its target to $900 and Bank of America to $732 on June 29, citing WDC's strategic positioning in AI storage infrastructure and data center capacity expansion cycles.
bear_case: Massive share dilution risk: the SanDisk spin-off transaction closed June 22, 2026, issuing ~21.3M new common shares, and insiders have recorded 125 sales vs. zero purchases over the past six months — a concerning signal.

HDD pricing expectations may be running ahead of likely actual gains (Fox Advisors downgrade to Equal-Weight), and the stock is trading near or above the published analyst consensus average, limiting near-term upside.

stocks.discussion_driver: CoreWeave dropped ~10.8% on July 1 after Bloomberg reported Meta Platforms is developing 'Meta Compute' — an initiative to sell its excess AI compute capacity externally, directly competing with neocloud providers. Meta represents approximately $35B (~35%) of CoreWeave's $99.4B revenue backlog, making customer concentration risk the central concern for investors. Evercore ISI maintained its Outperform rating at $150, noting existing locked-in contracts remain in force through 2032 and overall AI GPU demand remains robust across multiple customers.
bull_case: $99.4B contracted revenue backlog with long-term agreements from Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and OpenAI — including a $21B Meta AI infrastructure deal through December 2032 — provides exceptional revenue visibility even if Meta later redirects some demand.

Q1 FY2026 revenue doubled YoY to $2.08B, the company has 3.5+ GW of contracted power capacity under development, and 24 of 26 covering analysts maintain Buy ratings with median target of $145, implying 60%+ upside from current levels.
bear_case: Meta (~35% of total backlog) building its own external cloud business could simultaneously reduce future CoreWeave demand AND compete for the same enterprise customers — an existential double threat given the customer concentration.

CoreWeave carries heavy debt and capital costs to fund its GPU buildout; any slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, hyperscaler self-sufficiency shift, or loss of a major customer could rapidly compress margins and multiples.

stocks.discussion_driver: Abivax surged ~38% on June 30 after Phase 3 ABTECT Maintenance Part 2 trial data showed obefazimod achieving ~51% clinical remission at Week 44 versus 10.4% for placebo in treatment-refractory ulcerative colitis patients, with no new cancer safety signals over 44 weeks. Jefferies upgraded to Buy with a $158 price target, stating the data 'appropriately addresses the key safety overhang' — a malignancy signal at the 50mg dose that had weighed on the stock. Abivax plans to file an NDA with the FDA in Q4 2026, with Citizens Financial targeting $187 on the news.
bull_case: Phase 3 ABTECT data is compelling — ~51% remission vs 10.4% placebo in treatment-refractory patients across both induction and maintenance trials, with favorable 44-week safety profile, providing a clear regulatory path to NDA filing in Q4 2026.

First-in-class oral miR-124 enhancer mechanism differentiates obefazimod from existing biologics; multiple analysts (Jefferies $158, Citizens $187, Truist $135, Morgan Stanley $132) maintain Buy-equivalent ratings with average ~$148 target.
bear_case: FDA approval is not guaranteed — regulatory scrutiny of malignancy signals at the 50mg dose remains a key overhang, and any additional safety finding during the NDA review process could delay or derail the approval timeline.

Pre-revenue single-asset biotech concentration risk: failure of obefazimod or approval of a competing ulcerative colitis therapy (ozanimod, etrasimod) could dramatically reset the stock's valuation given the binary nature of the catalyst.
